summary: This Apache configuration file automatically redirects all incoming requests to use HTTPS and add 'www.' to the domain name if it's missing. It does this in two separate steps—first forcing HTTPS, then adding www—because some security certificate services prefer it that way.

explanations.1: This checks if Apache's mod_rewrite module is loaded; if it is, the rules inside will apply.
explanations.4: This turns on the rewrite engine, which allows Apache to modify URLs before serving pages.
explanations.7: This condition checks if the connection is NOT already using HTTPS (the secure protocol).
explanations.8: If the condition above is true, this rule rewrites the URL to use HTTPS while keeping the rest of the address the same; [L,R=301] means 'stop processing rules here (L) and send a permanent redirect (301)'.
explanations.12: This condition checks if the domain does NOT already start with 'www.'
explanations.13: If the condition above is true, this rule rewrites the URL to add 'www.' to the front of the domain.
